validation_gates.reason: evidence-resolution-record.yml runs only this validator and its tests, never the schema, so the validator is the only gate. It ignored the closed schema: a record with a recomputed record_id derived COMPLETE while carrying an extra effects.review_approved=true (an authority claim the contract classes as ERROR), an extra top-level or row field, a missing query_run_id, evaluated_at or reason_code, a non-date-time evaluated_at, a lowercase reason_code, a non-string bundle_id or integer refs. The CLI also printed a RecursionError traceback for deeply nested JSON, and --cases read its fixture relative to the working directory. The validator now validates the record against the paired schema (jsonschema and rfc3339-validator are core project dependencies, installed by the workflow) and reports SCHEMA_INVALID, catches RecursionError as INPUT_ERROR, and resolves the fixture from the repository root. Three of the new tests fail on the original code.

tests/validators/governance/test_evidence_resolution_record.py: 13 tests (7 before, 6 new) covering the closed-shape refusals, every semantic finding, the mixed-status outcome derivation (RESOLVED+DENIED is PARTIAL, UNRESOLVED+DENIED is UNRESOLVED), that every non-ERROR fixture satisfies the schema, and the CLI decisions and exit codes 0, 1 and 2 from any working directory. The test builds its own schema validator rather than trusting the module's. In-process branch coverage rises from 59% to 67%; the CLI paths run in subprocesses, which coverage does not measure. tests/validators/governance: 522 tests pass (516 before). All seven fixture cases keep their expected outcome and the semantic-only ERROR cases keep their exact findings.

Each of eleven changes failed the suite: removing the schema check or its format checker, the root-relative fixture path, the RecursionError handling, the coverage, row-ordering, DENIED, UNRESOLVED, digest-alphabet, record_id and profile checks.
